proposals.title: Topic: SIP units are taxed per instalment
proposals.change: Add topic 'Selling your SIP? Each instalment has its own holding period'. Inputs: monthly amount, months, assumed return, redemption month. Code computes how many instalments are over 12 months (long-term) and the split of gain; use current LTCG/STCG rates verified by the fact reviewer. Use quiz_countdown or myth_vs_fact.
evidence: https://www.oquilia.com/news/sip-post-tax-return-math-equity-ltcg
proposals.expectedEffect: Timely, specific topic; extra category variety (tax)
proposals.risk: Tax rates change; single secondary source, fact review must verify
proposals.reason: No template computes a per-instalment tax split, so this needs a new template before it can become a video.

proposals.title: Shock-number hook from record SIP inflows
proposals.change: Use a hook like 'Indians put Rs X cr into SIPs in one month' with X a dated constant in the script input, shown with its month and source; follow with a per-person SIP growth calculation computed by code.
evidence: https://www.oquilia.com/news/amfi-june-2026-sip-record-31781-crore
proposals.expectedEffect: Stronger first-second hook via a social-proof number
proposals.risk: Figure is gross and from a secondary source; becomes stale

proposals.title: Keep every video clearly original; watch the 'templated + synthetic voice' risk
proposals.change: No code yet. When 48h data exists, compare avgViewPct and impressions between voiceover on/off arms; if the narrated arm is limited or demonetised, the improver should reduce narration share. Until then keep template, palette and script variety as is.
evidence: https://www.netinfluencer.com/youtube-clarifies-july-15-policy-update-repetitious-content-rebranded-as-inauthentic-content/
https://www.androidheadlines.com/2026/07/youtube-monetization-rules-ai-slop-inauthentic-content.html
proposals.risk: Secondary sources disagree on 2026 details (templated content, AI personas advising on sensitive topics)

proposals.title: One quantity, one on-screen string across all beats
proposals.change: Add a check (number check or render gate) that every figure shown more than once in a video renders the identical string: chart end labels, counters and comparison bars must read the canonical maths value (e.g. maths.fv) rather than the last sampled chart point, and must use the same rounding and the same annuity convention. Fail the render with the beat names when two labels for the same key differ.
evidence: videos/v-20261017-04/preview.png: 15.9 s '₹6.5 L gone' vs 26.7 s 'Put in ₹6.4 L'; 26.7 s 'Worth ₹16.3 L' vs 32.2 s bar '₹16.5 L' (16.37 L is the end-of-month SIP value, 16.52 L the start-of-month one)
proposals.expectedEffect: No contradictory figures in one video: protects trust and the YMYL accuracy bar; a viewer pausing on two frames sees the same numbers.
proposals.risk: Low; may fail some renders until chart labels read the maths values.
proposals.note: 2026-10-18 improver: renderer/timeline/build.py _one_string() fails the script check and the build when a count-up/bar `value` lands on a `text` that does not show that same number, or when `value` is a typed number. On Remotion every other on-screen string already comes from one formatter per maths key, so the old-engine mismatch in v-20261017-04 cannot recur that way.

proposals.title: improvement.evaluate imports numpy, despite 'standard library only'
proposals.change: generator/variety.py imports BPM_RANGE, GENRES, KEYS from renderer/engine/music.py, which imports numpy at top level, so `python -m improvement.evaluate` fails on a plain Python 3.11 (ModuleNotFoundError: numpy). Move those three constants to a numpy-free module (e.g. renderer/engine/music_constants.py) re-exported by music.py, or import numpy lazily inside music.py's functions. Add a test that imports improvement.evaluate with numpy blocked.
evidence: Research run 2026-10-18: /usr/local/bin/python3 (3.11) → ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'numpy' from renderer/engine/music.py line 9; worked only with a Python that had numpy
proposals.expectedEffect: Agents get the evaluator ranking on any Python, as agents/research.md promises.
proposals.reason: Needs generator/variety.py (owner-only in scripts/guard.py) to stop importing renderer.engine.music; raised to the owner in improvement/notifications/improver.json. The improver runs the evaluator with a Python that has numpy meanwhile.

proposals.title: A recurring series tag for decision-duel Shorts (Rohan vs Priya)
proposals.change: For decision_duel Shorts only, on half the videos (flag), append a fixed series tag to the title, e.g. '… | Rohan vs Priya', and open the video with both characters on screen facing off over one concrete purchase in rupees (a ₹X car, a ₹Y home loan). The rest of the title must still pass the opening-phrase and shape rules on its own.
evidence: market.json 17 Oct: Mayank Gupta's '50 Lakh Home Loan | Rich Vs Middle Class Mindset' (147.7k views, 163 comments, 1.1 comments per 1,000 views) and '20 Lakh Toyota Innova Car | Rich Vs Middle Class Mindset' (49.8k, 1.8 per 1,000) — a recurring two-person duel on one concrete purchase, series tag as suffix; comment rates 5–20× Finance With Sharan's
proposals.expectedEffect: A recognisable series lifts returning viewers and comments; our cast already gives us the two people.
proposals.risk: A fixed suffix may read as templated (inauthentic-content risk) and could trip the title-shape rule; one channel is weak evidence.

proposals.title: Rotate the narrator voice per video instead of drawing it at random
proposals.change: renderer/timeline/build.py picks the narrator with random.Random(f'narrator:{seed}').choice(NARRATOR_VOICES), so voices repeat: am_michael narrated v-20261017-02, v-20261018-01, -02 and -03 (3 in a row on one day) and af_heart has never narrated a Remotion Short. Have the planner/writer step set the script's `narrator` to the least recently used voice in NARRATOR_VOICES (read from the last videos' render.json `voice.name` or a `narrator` field recorded in history), never the same as the previous video; build.py's seeded choice stays as the fallback. Add a test: four consecutive plans get four different narrators.
evidence: videos/v-20261017-02, v-20261018-01, v-20261018-02, v-20261018-03 render.json: voice.name = am_michael; v-20261017-04 af_bella; v-20261018-04 and L-20261018-01 am_fenrir; af_heart never used
CLAUDE.md hard constraints: voices 'rotated per video'; variety rules: rotate per video
proposals.expectedEffect: Each upload in a row sounds different, as CLAUDE.md requires; lowers the 'mass-produced' signal for viewers who see several Shorts back to back.
proposals.risk: None; only which of the already approved voices narrates.

proposals.title: The first spoken line says what frame 0 shows: no warm-up opener
proposals.change: On half the Shorts (flag), the writer's rule and check_script: the first beat's `say` must voice the stakes shown on screen at frame 0 (the hook question in the same words, or the hook figure's placeholder) within its first 8 words, and may not open with a warm-up phrase ('quick question', 'let's talk about', 'did you know', 'today', 'so'). Measure the first second on viewed-vs-swiped-away when available, else avgViewPct.
evidence: videos/v-20261018-02/script.json: frame 0 shows 'Is your savings account keeping up?' while the voice says 'Quick question about your savings.' (1.8 s, no figure, no stakes); the stakes arrive only in beat 2
https://shortsfast.com/blog/faceless-shorts-hooks-retention-2026/ (lead with the viewer's question and a specific answer; cut greetings; first frame matches the promise)
https://ads.tiktok.com/business/en-US/creative-codes (hook–body–close; the hook carries the promise)
https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/12942217 (viewed vs swiped away measures the first choice)
proposals.expectedEffect: Fewer swipes in the first second, where Shorts lose most viewers; our best openers (v-20261018-03 '₹56.0 L in interest. On just one home loan.') already do this.
proposals.risk: Low; a stricter opener could read formulaic if every video opens with a number, so questions count too.

proposals.title: New maths kinds for inflation stories: real return and price rise
proposals.change: Add two kinds to renderer/models/maths.py (and the number check's closed forms): `real_return` {amount, rate_pct, inflation_pct, years} → nominal final, real final in today's money ((1+r)/(1+i))^n, buying power lost, real rate; and `price_rise` {monthly, inflation_pct, years} → new monthly cost, extra per year, extra over N years. Document both in the long_story README's maths table with one example each.
evidence: Tonight's feed has three inflation/bills topics (US CPI energy 20.4%, UK price cap, UK CPI event day); v-20261018-02 and v-20261016-03 told inflation without a kind for it
improvement/events/2026-10-21-uk-cpi.json has to fake a price rise with `lumpsum`
proposals.expectedEffect: Inflation, bills and savings-vs-inflation stories (a recurring global news theme: CPI releases monthly in four countries) get honest labels and charts instead of investment-growth wording.
proposals.risk: Low; new kinds only, existing ones unchanged.

proposals.title: The narrator never shares a voice with a cast member who speaks in the same video
proposals.change: In generator/run.py where the narrator is set (next_narrator / the rotation at ~line 228), also give way when the narrator equals CAST_VOICES[s] for any beat speaker s in the script (renderer/timeline/build.py: sharma=am_fenrir, sikka=af_bella are also in NARRATOR_VOICES): pick the least recently used narrator that isn't one of those voices. Add a test: a script with a Sharma beat never gets am_fenrir as narrator. Optionally check_script fails a script whose explicit narrator clashes.
evidence: videos/v-20261018-04/render.json and videos/L-20261018-01/render.json: narrator am_fenrir while Sharma (am_fenrir) also speaks, so the narrator and Sharma sound identical
renderer/timeline/build.py comment: 'each recurring character always speaks with the same voice, so viewers know them by ear'
proposals.expectedEffect: Viewers can tell the narrator from Sharma/Sikka by ear; removes a confusing moment in about 1 video in 4 that uses Sharma or Sikka.

proposals.title: A short silence and a hit before the computed reveal (Shorts)
proposals.change: Behind flag `reveal-pause` (Shorts, 50%): on the beat whose scene shows the story's main computed result (the writer marks it `reveal: true`, else the first beat after the midpoint with a count-up), add 0.35 story-seconds of silence before the line (LEAD + 0.35), duck the music bed to near zero in that gap, and place an sfx 'hit' on the count-up's landing event. No change to words or numbers.
evidence: Our last 7 Shorts are voiced 86-90% of their runtime with 0.27-0.47 s between lines (render.json fills); there is no pause before any reveal

Explainer voiceover guides recommend pauses before key points and music ducked 6-12 dB under voice: https://voicebros.com/en/blog/explainer-video-voice-over-guide, https://skills.sh/1nfsh/s/explainer-video-guide
proposals.expectedEffect: The payoff number lands harder; might raise % viewed past the midpoint. Costs ~0.3 s of runtime.
proposals.risk: Slightly longer Shorts; a silence could read as a glitch if too long.
proposals.reason: Waits: sound area is taken by the running quiet-bed experiment.

proposals.title: Enforce the 'new picture every 3–5 s' rule inside long Shorts beats
proposals.change: In check_script (renderer/timeline/build.py) for format SHORT: after timing, any beat longer than 5 s must have a named event or camera move at least every 3 s of its length (counting the beat start and end); otherwise warn the writer to split the beat or add an event, and after the improver confirms no false positives on the last 10 scripts, make it a rewrite reason. Add a writer note in renderer/templates/short_story/README.md: 'a beat over 5 s needs an event every ≤3 s'.
evidence: CLAUDE.md render conventions: a new picture every 3–5 s (Shorts)
Our timelines v-20261019-01…v-20261020-03: 18 of 49 beats have a gap over 3 s with no event; 11 beats run over 6 s (longest 9.1 s, v-20261020-01 'year')
https://aibrify.com/en/blog/youtube-shorts-retention-curve-playbook
https://spliceapp.com/blog/mastering-youtube-shorts-editing-guide/
proposals.expectedEffect: Fewer visual pauses mid-Short; the liveliness gate passes already (median 1.25–2.30) but measures pixels, not new information.
proposals.risk: Writers split lines into choppy beats; keep the check on events, not beat count.

proposals.title: First picture change by 2 s: cap the hook beat at 4 s
proposals.change: Behind a flag (Shorts only): the first beat may last at most 4 s; if the hook line is longer, the writer splits it in two beats, or the first beat gets a camera punch or event at ≤2 s. On, the check rejects a longer first beat; off, today's behaviour. Start only after hook-voice-matches-frame has a verdict (both touch the first seconds).
evidence: Hook beats of the last 6 Shorts: 2.9, 3.9, 4.9, 5.4, 8.6, 3.0 s; v-20261020-02's contact sheet shows the same picture at 0 s and 5 s
https://aibrify.com/en/blog/youtube-shorts-retention-curve-playbook (30–50% of viewers leave between 1 and 3 s; vendor benchmark)
https://opus.pro/blog/ideal-youtube-shorts-length-format-retention
proposals.risk: Clashes with the running hook experiment if started together; wait for its verdict.

proposals.title: No scene leaves the lower half of the frame empty
proposals.change: Behind a flag, in remotion/src/scenes: headline shows its figure with the first spoken word (not after the subtitle), and headline, split and kinetic scenes put a cast reaction, Sikka or an icon in the lower half while the upper half holds the text, so no still shows more than half the frame as plain background.
evidence: v-20261020-02 contact sheet: at 10 s (headline) only a title and 'since mid-September' on an empty background; at 30 s (split) and 40 s (kinetic) two thirds of the frame empty
Top niche Shorts this week are character-led (Futurama, Family Guy, Fintech Neeraj's two-character duel in market.json, 18 Oct)
proposals.expectedEffect: Busier, more character-led frames; higher % viewed.
proposals.risk: Clutter, or text overlapping the cast; the layout probe catches overlaps.

proposals.title: A maths kind for income tax by bands (UK first, any currency)
proposals.change: Add kind income_tax_bands to renderer/models/maths.py: inputs income, allowance, bands [[upper, rate_pct], …]; outputs tax, take-home, marginal rate, and the same for a second income (e.g. after a pay rise) so a frozen-threshold story is computed. Mirror in the number check's closed form; one checked example script in short_story/README.md (UK 2026–27: £12,570 allowance, 20% to £50,270, 40% to £125,140).
evidence: https://www.gov.uk/income-tax-rates
Feed topic 2026-10-21-uk-budget-oct28-frozen-allowance (Budget on 28 Oct) cannot compute a tax figure today
Tax stories also needed for US brackets and Indian regimes (sip-tranche-tax-explainer, 16 Oct)
proposals.expectedEffect: Unlocks tax stories, a whole category we can't tell with computed numbers now.
proposals.risk: Rules differ by country (Scotland, US filing status, India regimes); the kind stays a generic band table and the script states the assumptions.
